This image shows a relief wood carving found mounted above a wooden door in Nils Stokbergs grave chamber at a church (Borgund?) in Ålesund, Norway. It shows Death tearing at Stokberg while wife an children are watching. The inscription is dutch (maybe the carver was dutch) and says: "Het. Wærelds. god. is. in. dit. levven: den. mensch. geleend. en. niet. gegeeven", meaning "Our worldly goods are life itself: Is lent to man, not given". Apparently this was somehow lost during the 1904 city fire of Ålesund, but has later been in storage.
